title: A filtered colimit of normal rings is normal
statement: Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $i\mapsto R_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative rings, with colimit $R=\varinjlim_IR_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If every $R_i$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $R$ is a normal ring. (No condition on the transition maps.)

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), stated there for a directed system; a filtered colimit is a directed colimit by Categories, Lemma Tag 0032 (categories-lemma-directed-category-system). Used in More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 06DI.

proof.text: *Reduction to one prime and the colimit of the localizations.* By the definition of a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] we must show that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Fix $\mathfrak p$, write $\iota_i:R_i\to R$ for the coprojections and put $\mathfrak p_i=\iota_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, a prime of $R_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime], $i\mapsto D_i:=(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ is a functor from the filtered category $I$ to commutative rings, with transition maps $D(a):D_i\to D_j$ induced by $R(a)$, and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with the maps $\kappa_i:D_i\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, $x/s\mapsto\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(s)$, is its colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Since $R_i$ is a normal ring, each $D_i$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. So it suffices to show: a filtered colimit $R_{\mathfrak p}=\varinjlim_ID_i$ of normal domains, which is moreover nonzero, is a normal domain (Stacks: 'we reduce to proving the statement of the lemma for normal domains').

*Common lifts.* Every finite family $x_1,\dots,x_m$ of elements of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ comes from one index: by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2), applied to the diagram $i\mapsto D_i$ of commutative $\mathbb Z$-algebras (= commutative rings), $x_l=\kappa_{i_l}(y_l)$ with $y_l\in D_{i_l}$; as $I$ is filtered there are an object $k$ and morphisms $a_l:i_l\to k$, and since $\kappa_k\circ D(a_l)=\kappa_{i_l}$ (cocone), $x_l=\kappa_k(D(a_l)(y_l))$ for all $l$. Moreover, if $y,y'\in D_k$ are lifts at a common index and $z\in D_k$ with $\kappa_k(z)=0$, then by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] there is $f:k\to k'$ with $D(f)(z)=0$, and the images $D(f)(y),D(f)(y')$ are again lifts of the same elements; so finitely many relations among the lifted elements that hold in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ hold already in some $D_{k'}$ (apply the zero criterion to each relation and pass to a common later index, again by filteredness).

*$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a domain.* (The Stacks proof leaves this part implicit.) $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so $1\neq0$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Let $x,y\in R_{\mathfrak p}$ with $xy=0$. By step 2 there are $k$ and $u,v\in D_k$ with $\kappa_k(u)=x$, $\kappa_k(v)=y$, and since $\kappa_k(uv)=xy=0$, after passing along some $f:k\to k'$ we may assume $uv=0$ in $D_k$. As $D_k$ is a domain (step 1), $u=0$ or $v=0$, hence $x=0$ or $y=0$.

*$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is integrally closed.* Let $K$ be the field of fractions of the domain $R_{\mathfrak p}$ (step 3); $R_{\mathfrak p}	o K$ is injective. Let $\xi\in K$ be a root of a monic polynomial $P(T)=T^n+c_1T^{n-1}+\dots+c_n$ with $c_1,\dots,c_n\in R_{\mathfrak p}$; write $\xi=a/b$ with $a,b\in R_{\mathfrak p}$, $b
e0$. Then $e:=a^n+c_1a^{n-1}b+\dots+c_nb^n=b^nP(a/b)=0$ in $K$, hence in $R_{\mathfrak p}$. By step 2 there are an index $k$ and $\alpha, eta,\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n\in D_k$ mapping under $\kappa_k$ to $a,b,c_1,\dots,c_n$ such that $\alpha^n+\gamma_1\alpha^{n-1} eta+\dots+\gamma_n eta^n=0$ in $D_k$ (this element maps to $e=0$; pass to a later index). Since $\kappa_k( eta)=b

eq0$. Dividing by $ eta^n$ in the field of fractions $\operatorname{Frac}(D_k)$ gives $P_k(\alpha/ eta)=0$ for the monic $P_k(T)=T^n+\gamma_1T^{n-1}+\dots+\gamma_n\in D_k[T]$. As $D_k$ is a normal domain (step 1) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $\alpha/ eta=r$ for some $r\in D_k$, i.e. $\alpha=r eta$ in $D_k$ (since $D_k	o\operatorname{Frac}(D_k)$ is injective). Applying the ring map $\kappa_k$: $a=\kappa_k(r)b$, so $\xi=a/b=\kappa_k(r)\in R_{\mathfrak p}$. (Stacks: 'we can find a (sufficiently large) $i$ such that $a,b$ come from $a_i,b_i$, $P$ comes from a monic $P_i$ and $P_i(a_i/b_i)=0$. Since $R_i$ is normal we see $a_i/b_i\in R_i$ and hence also $a/b\in R$.')

*Conclusion.* By steps 3 and 4, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a domain integrally closed in its field of fractions, i.e. a normal domain; as $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary, $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. The argument used only the filtered-colimit descriptions of steps 1-2, so no reduction from filtered to directed index categories (Categories, Lemma Tag 0032) is needed, and no condition on the transition maps is used.
